questions.question: What was the unknown element under aluminium called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eka-Aluminium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Eka-Aluminium** was the name given by Dmitri Mendeleev to the unknown element predicted to lie below aluminium in the periodic table.
 
• Mendeleev formulated this term based on his periodic law, where "Eka-" means "one beyond" in Sanskrit, indicating its position relative to aluminium.
 
• The element later discovered and identified as Eka-Aluminium is **Gallium (Ga)**, which was found in 1875 by French chemist Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran.
 
• Mendeleev accurately predicted various properties of Eka-Aluminium, including its atomic mass, density, melting point, and oxide formula.
 
• The discovery of Gallium validated Mendeleev’s periodic table and his concept of periodicity, strengthening the scientific acceptance of the table.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Law:**

 
 
• Mendeleev's periodic law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic masses.
 
• This law formed the basis for the organization of elements in the periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Gallium:**
 
 
• Gallium has an atomic number of 31 and is a soft, silvery metal.
 
• It melts at a low temperature of about 29.76°C, making it unique among metals.
 
• Gallium is used in semiconductors, LEDs, and solar panels.
 
 
 
• **Mendeleev's Predictions:**
 
 
• Mendeleev predicted the existence and properties of several elements that were unknown at the time, including Scandium (Eka-Boron), Gallium (Eka-Aluminium), and Germanium (Eka-Silicon).
 
• His predictions were based on gaps in his periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Validation of Periodic Table:**
 
 
• The discovery of elements like Gallium, which matched Mendeleev's predictions, confirmed the accuracy and utility of the periodic table.
 
• This established the periodic table as one of the most important tools in chemistry.

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary basis for allocating seats in the Rajya Sabha among various States and Union Territories in India?

options.text: Population of each state or union territory

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Population of each state or union territory**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajya Sabha**, the upper house of the Indian Parliament, allocates seats to states and union territories based on their **population**.
 
• The allocation is done in accordance with the provisions of **Article 80 of the Indian Constitution**, which determines the seat distribution.
 
• States with higher populations are allocated more seats, ensuring proportional representation.
 
• The population data used for this purpose is derived from the **1971 Census**, as per the **42nd Amendment of the Constitution**.
 
• As of now, the Rajya Sabha consists of **245 members**, with most representatives elected by the legislative assemblies of states and union territories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 80 of the Indian Constitution**:

 
 
• Specifies the composition of the Rajya Sabha, including representation from states, union territories, and nominated members.
 
• States are represented by members elected by their legislative assemblies using the **single transferable vote system**.
 
 
 
• **Allocation of Seats**:
 
 
• Each state is allocated seats in proportion to its population, ensuring equitable representation.
 
• Union territories such as Delhi and Puducherry are also represented, but with fewer seats.
 
 
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment**:
 
 
• Freezes the use of population data for seat allocation at the **1971 Census** level, to maintain uniformity.
 
 
 
• **Role of Rajya Sabha**:
 
 
• Acts as a federal chamber to represent the interests of states and union territories in the Parliament.
 
• Ensures that the voice of smaller states is not overshadowed in legislative processes.

questions.question: In February 2025, what was the protein isoform '1N4R tau' identified by the University of Cologne being explored for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Treating Alzheimer's disease**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **1N4R tau** is an isoform of the tau protein, which is primarily associated with neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer's disease.
 
• This isoform is characterized by having **four microtubule-binding repeat regions** and one N-terminal insertion, making it relevant for studying tauopathies.
 
• Research by the University of Cologne in February 2025 explored the role of 1N4R tau in the **pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease**, particularly its involvement in tau aggregation.
 
• 1N4R tau accumulation in brain cells leads to the formation of toxic **neurofibrillary tangles**, which are a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease.
 
• The study aimed to investigate potential therapeutic approaches to **mitigate tau-induced neurotoxicity** and slow disease progression.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tau Proteins:**

 
 
• Tau proteins are microtubule-associated proteins that stabilize microtubules in neurons.
 
• When tau proteins become hyperphosphorylated, they detach from microtubules and aggregate, leading to cell damage.
 
 
 
• **Neurofibrillary Tangles:**
 
 
• Neurofibrillary tangles are clumps of tau protein found in the brains of individuals with Alzheimer's disease.
 
• They disrupt neural communication, contributing to cognitive decline.
 
 
 
• **Alzheimer's Disease:**
 
 
• Alzheimer's is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by memory loss, cognitive impairment, and behavioral changes.
 
• It is associated with the accumulation of beta-amyloid plaques and tau tangles in the brain.
 
 
 
• **Therapeutic Exploration:**
 
 
• Current research focuses on targeting tau aggregation as a potential therapeutic approach for Alzheimer's disease.
 
• Strategies include tau inhibitors, immunotherapy, and enhancing tau clearance mechanisms.

questions.question: Which Indian state shares its border with Bhutan and Bangladesh?

• Located in the northeastern region of India, Assam plays a vital role in regional connectivity between India and its neighboring countries.
 
• Districts like **Udalguri, Baksa, and Chirang** share Assam's boundary with Bhutan, while districts like **Dhubri and Karimganj** touch the border with Bangladesh.
 
• Assam's strategic location facilitates trade and cultural exchange with Bhutan and Bangladesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical Importance of Assam:**

 
 
• Assam is part of the **Seven Sister States** in northeastern India, bordered by Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Meghalaya, and West Bengal.
 
• The state is known for its **Brahmaputra River**, which serves as a lifeline for agriculture and transportation.
 
 
 
• **Border with Bhutan:**
 
 
• Assam shares its northern boundary with Bhutan, a landlocked Himalayan kingdom.
 
• The Indo-Bhutan border is open, facilitating free movement of people and goods under the **Indo-Bhutan Friendship Treaty**.
 
 
 
• **Border with Bangladesh:**
 
 
• Assam’s border with Bangladesh is located to the south, with key border points like **Karimganj and Dhubri**.
 
• India and Bangladesh share a strong bilateral relationship, with Assam being a critical point for trade and transit.
 
 
 
• **Connectivity via Assam:**
 
 
• Assam is a gateway to northeastern India, connecting the region to the rest of the country through the **Siliguri Corridor** (also known as the Chicken's Neck).
 
• It serves as a hub for trade, transportation, and cultural exchanges between India and its neighbors.

questions.question: In Windows 10 File Explorer, how can you group files by their type?

options.text: Use the 'Sort by' option and select 'Name'
Rename all files with the same type
Use the 'Group by' option and select 'Type'

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Use the 'Group by' option and select 'Type'**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Windows 10 File Explorer, the **'Group by'** option allows you to organize files based on specific attributes such as **Type, Name, Date Modified, etc.**.
 
• To group files by their type, navigate to the **'Group by'** menu and select **'Type'**. Files will then be displayed in categories based on their file extensions.
 
• The **'Group by'** feature is accessible via the **right-click context menu** or the **'View' tab** on the ribbon toolbar of File Explorer.
 
• This feature is particularly useful for organizing and quickly locating files of the same type, such as images, documents, or videos.
 
• After grouping by type, you can further refine the organization by applying the **'Sort by'** option to arrange files within each group.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Group by vs. Sort by:**

 
 
• **'Group by'** organizes files into categories based on a selected attribute.
 
• **'Sort by'** arranges files in ascending or descending order within a folder.
 
 
 
• **File Type:**
 
 
• File type refers to the specific format or extension of a file (e.g., .jpg, .pdf, .docx).
 
• Grouping files by type helps users manage multiple formats in a single folder efficiently.
 
 
 
• **Accessing File Explorer Options:**
 
 
• To access the 'Group by' option, open File Explorer, navigate to the folder, and right-click on an empty space.
 
• Alternatively, use the **'View' tab** on the ribbon and select **'Group by'**.
 
 
 
• **Customization:**
 
 
• Users can customize the grouping criteria to other attributes like **Date, Size, Name, or Tags**.
 
• This flexibility ensures that File Explorer adapts to specific organizational needs.
 
 
 
• **Windows File Explorer:**
 
 
• File Explorer is the default file management utility in Windows operating systems.
 
• It provides a user-friendly interface for accessing, organizing, and managing files and folders.

• The **Singphos' Rebellion** is associated with the Singpho tribe, an ethnic group primarily found in the northeastern state of **Assam**.
 
• The rebellion was part of the resistance against British colonial rule in the 19th century, reflecting the tribal community's struggle for autonomy and freedom.
 
• It occurred during the early period of British expansion in Assam, when the Singphos opposed the East India Company's attempts to control their lands.
 
• Singphos are renowned for their warrior traditions and cultural heritage, and they played a significant role in resisting colonial exploitation.

• **Singpho Tribe:**

 
 
• The Singpho tribe belongs to the **Tibeto-Burman linguistic group** and is primarily found in Assam and Arunachal Pradesh in India.
 
• They are closely related to the Kachin people of Myanmar and share cultural and linguistic similarities.
 
 
 
• **Tea Cultivation in Assam:**
 
 
• The Singpho community is believed to have introduced tea plants in Assam, which were later commercialized by the British.
 
• Robert Bruce, a British merchant, reportedly discovered tea plants used by the Singphos in the early 19th century.

questions.question: Which output device is specifically designed to produce high-quality printed graphics and text?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inkjet Printer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inkjet printers** are designed to produce high-quality graphics and text by spraying tiny droplets of liquid ink directly onto paper.
 
• They are widely used for **photo printing** and professional documents due to their superior resolution, typically ranging from **300 to 1200 dpi (dots per inch)** or higher.
 
• Inkjet printers are ideal for **color printing**, making them suitable for posters, brochures, and high-quality images.
 
• These printers support a variety of media, including **photo paper, card stock, and specialty papers**.
 
• They are commonly used in homes and small offices due to their **affordability** and compact size.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dot Matrix Printers**:

 
 
• Dot matrix printers use a matrix of pins to strike an ink ribbon and create images or text on paper.
 
• They are suited for **low-cost, high-volume** printing but produce lower-quality output compared to inkjet printers.
 
 
 
• **Laser Printers**:
 
 
• Laser printers use toner powder and static electricity to produce high-quality text and graphics.
 
• They are faster and more cost-effective for large-scale printing but are generally less effective for high-quality photo printing.
 
 
 
• **Projectors**:
 
 
• Projectors are output devices used to display visuals on a larger screen but are not designed for producing printed graphics or text.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Printers**:
 
 
• Inkjet printers excel in color accuracy and resolution, making them ideal for professionals in graphic design and photography.
 
• While laser printers are more cost-effective for text-heavy documents, they are less versatile in high-quality color printing.

questions.question: Which feature of the phosphodiester bond contributes most to the overall negative charge of the DNA molecule?

options.text: The phosphate group’s ionisable oxygen atoms

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The phosphate group's ionisable oxygen atoms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• DNA molecules carry a** negative charge**, primarily due to the presence of the phosphate group in the phosphodiester backbone.
 
• The phosphate group contains **ionisable oxygen atoms** that are negatively charged at physiological pH.
 
• These negatively charged oxygen atoms contribute to the **overall negative charge of the DNA molecule**, which affects its interactions with proteins, cations, and other molecules.
 
• The negative charge of DNA is critical for its **structural stability and biological functions**, such as in its interaction with histones and its electrophoretic mobility during gel-based experiments.
 
• Other components of DNA, such as the nitrogenous bases and the sugar, do not contribute significantly to the molecule's overall charge.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phosphodiester Bond:**

 
 
• A phosphodiester bond is a chemical bond formed between the 3'-hydroxyl group of one sugar and the phosphate group attached to the 5'-carbon of another sugar in the DNA or RNA backbone.
 
• This bond is crucial for the formation of the DNA and RNA polymer structure.
 
 
 
• **Role of Negative Charge in DNA:**
 
 
• The negative charge on DNA facilitates its interaction with positively charged proteins such as histones, which help in DNA packaging in chromatin.
 
• It also allows the DNA to migrate towards the positive electrode during electrophoresis, a common laboratory technique for DNA analysis.
 
 
 
• **Physiological pH:**
 
 
• The ionisation of the phosphate group occurs at physiological pH (~7.4), ensuring the DNA remains negatively charged under normal biological conditions.
 
 
 
• **Other Components of DNA:**
 
 
• The nitrogenous bases (adenine, thymine, cytosine, guanine) and the deoxyribose sugar are neutral and do not contribute to the overall charge of the DNA molecule.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about the Permanent Lok Adalat under Section 22-B of The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987?

options.text: The award of the Permanent Lok Adalat is not binding on the parties.
The Permanent Lok Adalat can handle cases up to a certain monetary limit (currently ₹1 crore).
The Permanent Lok Adalat can only act as a conciliator and cannot decide disputes.
The Permanent Lok Adalat has jurisdiction over disputes related to criminal offences.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Permanent Lok Adalat can handle cases up to a certain monetary limit (currently ₹1 crore)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Permanent Lok Adalat (PLA) is established under **Section 22-B of The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**.
 
• The PLA has jurisdiction over disputes related to **public utility services** like transport, postal, telecommunication, electricity, etc.
 
• The monetary limit for cases handled by the Permanent Lok Adalat is **₹1 crore**, as per the latest regulations.
 
• The PLA has the power to decide disputes if the parties fail to reach a settlement through conciliation.
 
• The award passed by the Permanent Lok Adalat is **final and binding** on the parties and is treated as a decree of a civil court.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conciliation Mechanism:** The PLA primarily focuses on conciliating disputes and tries to bring parties to a mutually acceptable solution without litigation.
 
• **Public Utility Services:** These include essential services like water supply, electricity, transport, postal services, telecommunication, and other utilities as defined under the Act.
 
• **Binding Nature of Awards:** Awards made by Permanent Lok Adalats are treated as final and binding, making them cost-effective and time-saving alternatives to litigation.
 
• **Difference from Lok Adalats:** Unlike Lok Adalats, Permanent Lok Adalats have the authority to decide disputes even if conciliation efforts fail.
 
• **Exclusion of Criminal Offences:** The Permanent Lok Adalat does not have jurisdiction over disputes related to criminal offences or cases outside the scope of public utility services.

questions.question: As per the SDG India Index 2023-24, what was the estimated percentage of reduction in the population living in multidimensional poverty between 2015-16 and 2019-21?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**From 24.8% to 14.96%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **SDG India Index 2023-24** highlights significant progress made by India in reducing multidimensional poverty.
 
• The percentage of the population living in multidimensional poverty reduced from **24.8% in 2015-16** to **14.96% in 2019-21**, showcasing a remarkable improvement.
 
• This reduction is in alignment with India’s commitment to achieving the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 1**, which focuses on ending poverty in all its forms.
 
• The achievement reflects the impact of various government initiatives, including improved healthcare, education, and living standards for economically weaker sections.
 
• The progress was measured using the **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**, which accounts for deprivations in health, education, and standard of living.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• The MPI is a measure developed by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** and the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)** to evaluate poverty beyond income, considering factors like health, education, and standard of living.
 
• It identifies individuals as “multidimensionally poor” if they experience deprivations in at least one-third of the weighted indicators.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• The SDGs are a set of 17 goals adopted by all United Nations Member States in 2015 to address global challenges, including poverty, inequality, climate change, and peace.
 
• **Goal 1** aims to "End poverty in all its forms everywhere."
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Reduce Poverty in India:**
 
 
• Programs like **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)**, **Ayushman Bharat**, and **National Food Security Act** have played a crucial role in improving living standards.
 
• Skill development schemes like **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)** aim to enhance employment opportunities.
 
 
 
• **India’s Progress on SDG 1:**
 
 
• India’s reduction in multidimensional poverty is a key indicator of its progress on SDG 1.
 
• Efforts have been focused on improving healthcare, education, and basic amenities to uplift marginalized communities.

questions.question: What is the central theme of the first five anthologies (Kuruntokai, Narrinai, Akananuru, Ainkurunuru, and Kalittokai) of the Ettuttokai in the Sangam literature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Akam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first five anthologies of the Ettuttokai in Sangam literature are part of the **Akam** category, which deals with themes of love and personal emotions.
 
• Akam poetry focuses on the inner, emotional, and personal aspects of human life, specifically romantic relationships, without direct reference to external societal events.
 
• Each anthology in this category portrays different aspects of love, such as longing, separation, union, and misunderstandings.
 
• The poems use symbolic landscapes, known as "tinai," to represent emotional states and situations, such as mountains for union and deserts for separation.
 
• The Akam theme is central to Tamil Sangam literature, emphasizing the intimate and universal emotions of love and relationships.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangam Literature:**

 
 
• Sangam literature is one of the oldest known Tamil literary traditions, dating back to 300 BCE–300 CE.
 
• It is broadly divided into two themes: **Akam** (inner life, love) and **Puram** (outer life, valor, and society).
 
 
 
• **Ettuttokai:**
 
 
• It is a collection of eight anthologies of Sangam poetry, divided into Akam (love) and Puram (valor).
 
• The first five anthologies (Kuruntokai, Narrinai, Akananuru, Ainkurunuru, and Kalittokai) fall under the Akam category.
 
 
 
• **Tinai Concept:**
 
 
• In Akam poetry, tinai refers to symbolic landscapes used to depict specific emotions and situations in love.
 
• Examples include **kurinji** (mountains for union) and **palai** (deserts for separation).
 
 
 
• **Puram Literature:**
 
 
• Puram focuses on themes of heroism, ethics, and public life, contrasting with the personal nature of Akam poetry.
 
 
 
• **Importance:**
 
 
• Sangam literature provides insights into the ancient Tamil society, its values, traditions, and emotional depth.

questions.question: What is the standard method to save your work in PowerPoint?

questions.question: Which seasonal change marks the withdrawal of monsoon in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Southward shift of ITCZ**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The withdrawal of monsoon in India is marked by the **southward shift of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ).**
 
• The ITCZ is a belt of low pressure near the equator where the trade winds converge and plays a crucial role in the monsoon system.
 
• During the withdrawal phase, the ITCZ shifts southward towards the equator, signaling the end of the rainy season.
 
• Withdrawal typically starts in northwest India by early October and progresses southward across the country.
 
• This shift is accompanied by clear skies, a reduction in humidity, and a rise in daytime temperatures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ):**

 
 
• The ITCZ is a dynamic region of low pressure near the equator formed by the convergence of northeast and southeast trade winds.
 
• It shifts northward and southward seasonally due to the apparent movement of the sun.
 
• Its position influences the monsoon rains in tropical regions, including India.
 
 
 
• **Indian Monsoon System:**
 
 
• The Indian monsoon is divided into two phases: **onset** (arrival) and **withdrawal** (retreat).
 
• The monsoon onset is driven by the northward movement of the ITCZ, while its withdrawal is linked to the southward shift.
 
 
 
• **Withdrawal of Monsoon:**
 
 
• The withdrawal process begins in northwest India and progresses southward, completing by November.
 
• It is marked by clear skies, reduced rainfall, and a gradual cooling of temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Polar Jet Streams:**
 
 
• These high-altitude winds influence weather patterns but are not directly linked to the withdrawal of the Indian monsoon.

questions.question: What is the term duration for representatives in municipalities in India?

__
 
• In India, representatives elected to municipalities serve a term of **5 years** as per the provisions of the **74th Constitutional Amendment Act**.
 
• Municipal elections are held at regular intervals to ensure democratic governance at the urban local level.
 
• During their tenure, municipal representatives oversee urban development projects, sanitation, water supply, and other civic amenities.
 
• If the municipality is dissolved before completing its 5-year term, elections must be conducted within **6 months** to reconstitute it.
 
• The **State Election Commission** is responsible for conducting municipal elections in each state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **74th Constitutional Amendment Act (1992):**

 
 
• This act provided the constitutional framework for urban local governance in India, including municipalities.
 
• It categorized municipalities into three types: Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils, and Municipal Corporations based on population and area.
 
• The act mandates the creation of Ward Committees in urban areas with a population of 3 lakh or more.
 
 
 
• **State Election Commission:**
 
 
• Established under Article 243K of the Constitution to oversee elections to municipalities and panchayats.
 
• Each state has its own Election Commission responsible for ensuring free and fair local elections.
 
 
 
• **Municipal Governance Functions:**
 
 
• Municipalities are responsible for urban planning, regulation of land use, water supply, sanitation, and public health.
 
• They play a crucial role in maintaining public infrastructure like roads, street lighting, and parks.
 
 
 
• **Urban Local Bodies Financing:**
 
 
• Municipalities receive funds from property taxes, grants from the state and central governments, and user charges for services.
 
• They also raise revenue through issuing municipal bonds in some cases.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers flows through Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Luni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Luni River** is the largest river in the Thar Desert region and primarily flows through the state of **Rajasthan, India**.
 
• The river originates from the **Aravalli Hills** near Ajmer and flows southwest into the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.
 
• Luni is known as a **saline river** because its water becomes increasingly brackish as it flows through arid regions.
 
• Despite its salinity, the river is an important water source for irrigation and local communities in Rajasthan.
 
• Luni does not drain into any ocean or sea but ends in marshy lands, making it an **endorheic river system**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rivers of Rajasthan:**

 
 
• Other important rivers in Rajasthan include **Chambal, Banas, and Mahi**, but these flow through multiple states.
 
• Luni is unique as it is **entirely confined to arid and semi-arid regions.**
 
 
 
• **Endorheic Basin:**
 
 
• An endorheic basin is a closed drainage system where water does not flow out to seas or oceans.
 
• The Luni River ends in the marshy lands of the Rann of Kutch, making it a classic example of such a system.
 
 
 
• **Salinity of Luni:**
 
 
• The river's water becomes increasingly saline due to the high evaporation rate and the geological makeup of the region.
 
• This salinity renders the water unsuitable for drinking but still usable for certain types of irrigation.
 
 
 
• **Other Rivers Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Jhelum:** Flows through Jammu & Kashmir and is part of the Indus River system.
 
• **Teesta:** Flows through Sikkim and West Bengal, eventually merging with the Brahmaputra in Bangladesh.
 
• **Tapi:** Originates in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward into the Arabian Sea.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Small Causes Courts is correct?

options.text: They can hear appeals from Nyaya Panchayats.

Their decisions are final but subject to High Court’s revision.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Small Causes Courts are established to deal with civil cases of a minor financial value, ensuring quick and cost-effective justice.
 
• The decisions of Small Causes Courts are final; however, they can be revised by the High Court under its supervisory jurisdiction.
 
• These courts do not deal with criminal cases; their jurisdiction is limited to specific minor civil disputes like property disputes or money recovery cases.
 
• Small Causes Courts are governed by the provisions of the **Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887**, in states where they exist.
 
• They do not operate under uniform nomenclature across all states; their presence and structure vary depending on state-specific laws.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887:** This Act governs the establishment and functioning of Small Causes Courts, outlining their jurisdiction and procedures.
 
• **Jurisdiction:** These courts typically handle civil cases involving amounts up to a specified financial limit (varies by state) and exclude cases like marriage disputes, testamentary matters, etc.
 
• **High Court Supervision:** While their decisions are final, High Courts can revise decisions if there is a procedural irregularity or legal error.
 
• **Appeals:** Appeals from Small Causes Courts are not generally allowed unless specified under the law, emphasizing their role in quick dispute resolution.
 
• **Presence of Small Causes Courts:** They are more common in urban areas where minor civil disputes are frequent, ensuring faster resolution of such matters.

questions.question: Which is NOT an advantage of a Lok Adalat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to appeal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lok Adalat decisions are **final and binding** on both parties, ensuring disputes do not escalate further.
 
• There is **no provision for an appeal** against the decision made in a Lok Adalat to maintain efficiency and avoid prolonged litigation.
 
• Lok Adalats are known for **speedy resolution** of disputes, avoiding lengthy court procedures.
 
• They provide **cost-effective justice** by eliminating court fees and reducing financial burden on litigants.
 
• Lok Adalats aim to resolve disputes through **mutual consent and compromise**, promoting harmony between parties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **What is Lok Adalat?**

 
 
• Lok Adalat, meaning "People's Court," is a statutory mechanism under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
 
• It resolves disputes through **conciliation and compromise**, without a formal judicial trial.
 
• It is aimed at reducing the burden on regular courts and providing quick justice.
 
 
 
• **Legal Basis:**
 
 
• The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 empowers Lok Adalats to resolve civil, matrimonial, and compoundable criminal cases.
 
• Its primary focus is on disputes where parties are willing to resolve issues amicably.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Lok Adalat:**
 
 
• Lok Adalats help reduce the backlog of cases in courts.
 
• They provide free and speedy justice, ensuring accessibility for economically weaker sections.
 
• There is no strict adherence to procedural laws, making the process informal and efficient.
 
 
 
• **Limitations:**
 
 
• Decisions are binding and final, meaning no further appeal can be made.
 
• Lok Adalats can only handle cases where both parties agree to a settlement; contested cases are referred back to regular courts.
